I've been farming this land for 40 years. My father taught me, and his father taught him. I know this soil. I know when to plant and when to water. I don't need papers from a school to tell me what to do with my own land.

My 12 mu breaks down like this: I keep 8 mu for the wheat-maize rotation — that's my main food crop income. The other 4 mu I put in cotton, same as always. Cotton is hard work but the cash is good if the weather holds.

For wheat this winter, I'll plough deep like always before planting. I'll use the improved seed from the county station — my neighbor used it last year and got a good yield. I'll put down base fertilizer at planting, then top-dress at jointing. I irrigate four times: once at sowing to get germination, once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Two rounds of pesticide — one for rust, one for aphids. I expect around 450 jin per mu if heaven is kind.

For summer maize, I don't replough — just rotary till after wheat harvest, it's faster and the season is tight. Hybrid seed, everyone uses it now. Same fertilizer habit as wheat more or less. Three irrigations. Yield should be around 550 jin.

For cotton, I plough in spring. I'll use improved Bt seed to cut down on bollworm spray, but I still spray 6 times — aphids, spider mites, other pests. Cotton drinks a lot of water, I irrigate 5 times from my well. Cotton is the crop that gives me cash money before the year-end.
